title: Title and 1st Point: Discipline and Gratitude Lesson for the Commanding Self

questions.question: What warning is given at the beginning about people who feel happy about what they arranged and want praise for things they did not do?
questions.answer: They should not think they are safe from punishment, because painful punishment awaits them.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to in the passage after the opening warning?
questions.answer: The speaker is talking to his own self, especially the part that pushes toward wrong.

questions.question: What bad qualities of the self are listed?
questions.answer: It loves attention, wants a big name, likes praise, and is full of ego.

questions.question: What example is used to show where fruit really comes from?
questions.answer: The passage points to a tiny seed for figs and a vine branch carrying grapes.

questions.question: Why do those examples weaken the self’s claim to be proud?
questions.answer: They show that what appears to carry or show blessings is not the true owner or maker of them.

questions.question: According to the passage, what power makes the self more blameworthy than a seed or branch?
questions.answer: It has a will and makes wrong choices.

questions.question: How does pride harm blessings?
questions.answer: It lowers their value.

questions.question: What does ingratitude do to blessings?
questions.answer: It wipes out their benefit.

questions.question: What is wrong with acting as if blessings belong to oneself?
questions.answer: It is like taking what is not rightfully yours.

questions.question: Instead of showing off actions, what should a person do?
questions.answer: A person should thank Allah.

questions.question: Instead of seeking fame, what quality should a person choose?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: Instead of wanting praise, what should a person seek?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking Allah for forgiveness.

questions.question: Where does true human perfection lie, according to the passage?
questions.answer: In knowing Allah, not in being focused on oneself.

questions.question: What is the similarity between the human self and nature in the world?
questions.answer: Both receive good and are places where evil is linked, rather than being the true source of good.

questions.question: What is the only effect the self is said to have?
questions.answer: It becomes a cause for evil by failing to receive good in the right way.

questions.question: Why were the self and nature made as veils?
questions.answer: So that things whose beauty is hidden could be connected to them, while Allah remains known as free from defect.

questions.question: What serious mistake happens when a person worships the self or nature?
questions.answer: That person acts with great foolishness and commits a serious wrong.

questions.question: Why is the self told not to claim beauty just because beauty appears through it?
questions.answer: Because it has not truly taken that beauty into itself; it only lets it pass through.

questions.question: Why is the self told not to think being chosen among people proves its worth?
questions.answer: Because gifts may be given first to the one who is most needy, weak, and sad.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: People should not be proud of blessings or good works, but should be humble, thankful, and aware that all goodness comes from Allah.

questions.question: What kind of people are warned of painful suffering in the opening verse?
questions.answer: People who delight in what they managed and want credit for things they never did.

questions.question: Why is the passage called a chastening message to the self?
questions.answer: Because it corrects and scolds the self for pride and false claims.

questions.question: Which part of a person is especially being corrected here?
questions.answer: The commanding self that pushes toward wrong desires.

questions.question: What two plant examples are used to teach a lesson about blessings?
questions.answer: A fig seed and a grape vine branch.

questions.question: If the self were really like the true maker of fruit, what might it claim?
questions.answer: It might claim a right to feel proud.

questions.question: Why does the passage reject that claim?
questions.answer: Because the self is not the true source of the blessings it carries.

questions.question: How does the self’s free choice make its fault greater?
questions.answer: It uses choice in a bad way and damages what it receives.

questions.question: What happens to blessings when a person becomes conceited?
questions.answer: Their worth is spoiled.

questions.question: How is ingratitude described in its effect on blessings?
questions.answer: It makes them empty and useless.

questions.question: What does it mean to wrongfully claim blessings as your own?
questions.answer: It means acting like you own what Allah gave.

questions.question: What should replace bragging about deeds?
questions.answer: Gratitude to Allah.

questions.question: What should replace the desire for fame?
questions.answer: Modesty.

questions.question: What should replace the desire to be praised?
questions.answer: Turning back to Allah and asking His forgiveness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes a person truly complete?
questions.answer: Realizing Allah and not living around the ego.

questions.question: In what way are the self and nature passive rather than active?
questions.answer: They receive what is given and are not the real creators of good.

questions.question: How can the self become connected to evil?
questions.answer: By failing to welcome good as it should.

questions.question: What purpose do the veils of self and nature serve?
questions.answer: They are places where outwardly unpleasant things are attached, so Allah is known to be free from faults.

questions.question: What wrong attitude is compared to acting like a partner with the Creator?
questions.answer: Turning good into evil and then claiming a share in what belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: Why is self-worship described as very foolish?
questions.answer: Because it gives created things a place they do not deserve.

questions.question: What answer is given to the idea, “Beauty appeared through me, so I must be beautiful”?
questions.answer: Showing beauty is not the same as owning it or becoming worthy by yourself.

questions.question: Why might gifts be given first to someone in great need?
questions.answer: Because that person is poorer, weaker, and more in need of help.

questions.question: What feeling does the speaker express after seeing the self silenced?
questions.answer: Great happiness and strong approval.

questions.question: What false hope is denied in the verse at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The hope of escaping punishment while loving undeserved praise.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about enjoying praise for work you did not do?
questions.answer: It is blameworthy and dangerous.

questions.question: What kind of self is being warned and corrected?
questions.answer: A proud self that loves status and praise.

questions.question: Why are a seed and a vine branch mentioned?
questions.answer: They help explain that carrying blessings does not mean making them.

questions.question: What mistake would the self make if it copied the seed or branch in the wrong way?
questions.answer: It would think it deserves all the credit for what appears through it.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the self deserves rebuke?
questions.answer: Because it misuses its will and responds wrongly to blessings.

questions.question: What is one way pride changes the value of blessings?
questions.answer: It makes them less valuable.

questions.question: What is one way thanklessness affects blessings?
questions.answer: It cancels their good.

questions.question: Why is claiming blessings for oneself compared to taking something unlawfully?
questions.answer: Because those blessings really belong to Allah, not to the person.

questions.question: Name one duty of the self mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: To give thanks.

questions.question: Name another duty of the self mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: To be humble.

questions.question: What spiritual actions are said to be a person’s right instead of praise?
questions.answer: Repentance and seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: How does the passage define perfection in a believer?
questions.answer: It is found in recognizing Allah, not in ego.

questions.question: What common role do the self and nature have regarding good?
questions.answer: They receive it rather than produce it.

questions.question: What common role do the self and nature have regarding evil?
questions.answer: Evil is connected to them as a result of their failure.

questions.question: Why are hiddenly ugly things linked to self and nature?
questions.answer: So Allah’s purity from faults is understood.

questions.question: What happens when the self goes against its created duty?
questions.answer: It behaves opposite to its purpose and acts as if it shares in Allah’s work.

questions.question: Why should the self not say, “I was the place where beauty showed up, so I deserve beauty”?
questions.answer: Because beauty passing through something does not prove that thing owns or absorbs it.

questions.question: How does the passage answer the idea that being chosen shows personal greatness?
questions.answer: It says gifts can come first to the one in greatest need, not the one with greatest merit.

questions.question: What view of oneself does the passage encourage?
questions.answer: A believer should see himself as needy before Allah, not as impressive on his own.

questions.question: What behavior in the opening verse is connected with punishment?
questions.answer: Feeling proud of one’s plotting and wanting applause for things not actually done.

questions.question: Why does the speaker call the self foolish?
questions.answer: Because it chases honor, fame, and praise in a proud way.

questions.question: What do the fruit examples teach about where success comes from?
questions.answer: Success and blessings come from a true giver, not from the object that merely carries them.

questions.question: If a branch carries grapes, does that make it the real owner of the harvest? Explain.
questions.answer: No. It is only a means through which the grapes appear.

questions.question: Why is the self said to deserve blame again and again?
questions.answer: Because it acts proudly even though it should be thankful and humble.

questions.question: How does human choice make the self more responsible than a seed?
questions.answer: A seed has no will, but the self can choose wrongly.

questions.question: What does pride do to the blessings a person has?
questions.answer: It reduces their worth.

questions.question: What does conceit do to those blessings?
questions.answer: It ruins them.

questions.question: What does ingratitude do to them?
questions.answer: It removes their benefit.

questions.question: What is wrong with saying, “These blessings are mine by my own power”?
questions.answer: It is like grabbing what belongs to Allah.

questions.question: What should a Muslim do with good deeds and blessings instead of boasting?
questions.answer: Thank Allah for them.

questions.question: Which is better in this passage: fame or humility?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: Which is better in this passage: praise from people or repentance before Allah?
questions.answer: Repentance before Allah.

questions.question: What is better for a person: self-centeredness or knowing Allah?
questions.answer: Knowing Allah.

questions.question: Why are the self and nature described as not being true doers?
questions.answer: Because they are receivers, not creators of good.

questions.question: How can evil become attached to the self?
questions.answer: By its bad response to good.

questions.question: Why were self and nature made as coverings or veils?
questions.answer: So outwardly unpleasant matters can be connected to them while Allah is known to be perfect.

questions.question: What big mistake does a person make by worshipping nature or the self?
questions.answer: The person gives created things a place that belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: Why is being a channel for beauty not proof of personal excellence?
questions.answer: Because a channel only passes something along.

questions.question: What reason is given for being chosen to receive gifts first?
questions.answer: Greater need and poverty, not greater greatness.

questions.question: What attitude should this passage build in a believer’s heart?
questions.answer: Thankfulness, repentance, humility, and dependence on Allah.

questions.question: What are people wrongly happy about in the opening warning?
questions.answer: They are pleased with what they brought about and enjoy praise they did not earn.

questions.question: What end awaits such people if they do not repent?
questions.answer: Painful punishment.

questions.question: What four traits of the self are criticized early in the passage?
questions.answer: Loving glory, wanting fame, being attached to praise, and being full of ego.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a tiny beginning for a fig tree and a dry branch for grapes?
questions.answer: To show that something small or weak may carry results without being the true owner of them.

questions.question: What lesson should the self learn from those examples?
questions.answer: It should not become proud over blessings shown through it.

questions.question: Why does the self deserve even more correction than a plant part?
questions.answer: Because it has a will and still misuses blessings.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of pride?
questions.answer: It lowers the worth of blessings.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of conceit?
questions.answer: It destroys blessings.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of thanklessness?
questions.answer: It cancels blessings.

questions.question: How is taking credit for blessings described morally?
questions.answer: It is treated like taking what is not yours.

questions.question: What is the self’s duty regarding blessings?
questions.answer: To thank Allah.

questions.question: What character quality fits the self better than public honor?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What worshipful response fits the self better than being praised by people?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking forgiveness.

questions.question: What kind of perfection is rejected in the passage?
questions.answer: Perfection based on self-centeredness.

questions.question: What kind of perfection is accepted in the passage?
questions.answer: Perfection based on knowing Allah.

questions.question: In what way are the self and nature alike?
questions.answer: Both receive good but are linked with evil in a secondary way.

questions.question: What does the passage say they are not?
questions.answer: They are not the real actors or sources.

questions.question: What role do they have in relation to ugly-looking things whose wisdom is hidden?
questions.answer: They serve as screens to which such things are outwardly attributed.

questions.question: What does going against that role lead to?
questions.answer: Acting as if one shares in Allah’s creative work.

questions.question: What answer is given to someone who says, “Beautiful works appeared through me, so I must have merit”?
questions.answer: The gifts came not because of merit, but because of greater need and poverty.

questions.question: What is one strong summary sentence for the passage?
questions.answer: Do not praise yourself for Allah’s gifts; be humble, thankful, and repentant.

questions.question: What kind of praise is condemned in the opening verse?
questions.answer: Praise for things a person did not actually do.

questions.question: What does the verse say such people should not expect?
questions.answer: Safety from punishment.

questions.question: What inner enemy is being corrected in this passage?
questions.answer: The selfish inner side that commands toward wrong.

questions.question: Which desires of that inner self are named?
questions.answer: It wants glory, fame, and praise.

questions.question: What do the examples of fruits teach about cause and result?
questions.answer: The thing we see holding the result is not always the true maker of it.

questions.question: If someone receives blessings through himself, does that mean he made them?
questions.answer: No, it does not.

questions.question: Why is the self especially responsible for its mistakes?
questions.answer: Because it has the ability to choose.

questions.question: What does the passage say pride does to blessings?
questions.answer: It cheapens them.

questions.question: What does the passage say ingratitude does to blessings?
questions.answer: It erases their value.

questions.question: Why is ownership language about blessings dangerous?
questions.answer: Because it steals credit from Allah.

questions.question: What should replace showing off good deeds?
questions.answer: Thanking Allah.

questions.question: What should replace chasing a big name?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What should replace wanting compliments?
questions.answer: Repenting and asking Allah to forgive.

questions.question: How should a believer understand true excellence?
questions.answer: True excellence comes from recognizing Allah, not praising oneself.

questions.question: What shared condition do the self and nature have in relation to good?
questions.answer: They are receivers, not original sources.

questions.question: What shared condition do they have in relation to evil?
questions.answer: Evil is attached to them because of deficiency and failure.

questions.question: Why were they created as coverings?
questions.answer: To carry the outward side of things whose hidden beauty is not obvious, while Allah is known to be perfect.

questions.question: What does the passage say about worshipping the self or nature?
questions.answer: It is extreme foolishness and a serious injustice.

questions.question: Why can’t a person claim beauty just because beauty appeared through him?
questions.answer: Because he may only be a pathway, not a true possessor of that beauty.

questions.question: What is the real reason given for being selected for gifts?
questions.answer: Being more needy, poor, and broken, not being better than others.

questions.question: How can this passage help a Muslim student in daily life?
questions.answer: It teaches the student to avoid bragging, thank Allah for success, and stay humble when praised.
